activeElements.body:
Allow party members to describe how they help cross the river, using Action Rolls to tick down the _Cross the River_ counter.

Since _Undertow_ is more situational than _Patient Hunter_, use it as soon as the narrative supports someone being in the water and you get a GM Move.

_Patient Hunter_ is best used when a character is within Close of some greenery, which is easily done on the map. A snake coming out of the bushes makes good sense. _Spinning Serpent_ attacks targets in Very Close, so it will need to move first. Try to position the _Glass Snake_ to affect multiple characters.

Spend an extra Fear on _Patient Hunter_ to summon a Bear instead of a Glass Snake.

Using _Patient Hunter_ on the same character as _Undertow_ also makes narrative sense as the character is swept into the hunter's domain.

If the party just isn't rolling with Fear, you can spend a Fear to steal the spotlight and make a GM move.
activeElements.name: Running Raging River
Glass Snake

features.name: Armor-Shredding Shards
features.description: After a successful attack against the Snake within Melee range, the attacker must mark an Armor Slot. If they can't mark an Armor Slot, they must mark an HP.

features.name: Spinning Serpent
features.description: **Mark a Stress** to make an attack against all targets within Very Close range. Targets the Snake succeeds against take **1d6+1** physical damage.

features.name: Spitter
features.description: **Spend a Fear** to introduce a **d6** Spitter Die. When the Snake is in the spotlight, roll this die. On a result of 5 or higher, all targets in front of the Snake within Far range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take **1d4** physical damage. The Snake can take the spotlight a second time this GM turn.

activeElements.description: A clear serpent with a massive head that leaves behind a glass shard trail wherever they go.

activeElements.name: Raging River

features.name: Dangerous Crossing
features.description: Crossing the river requires the party to complete a Progress Countdown (4). A PC who rolls a failure with Fear is immediately targeted by the "Undertow" action without requiring a Fear to be spent on the feature. _Have any of the PCs forded rivers like this before? Are any of them afraid of drowning?_

features.name: Undertow
features.description: **Spend a Fear** to catch a PC in the undertow. They must make an Agility Reaction Roll. On a failure, they take **1d6+1** physical damage and are moved a Close distance down the river, becoming _Vulnerable_ until they get out of the river. On a success, they must mark a Stress. _What trinkets and baubles lie along the bottom of the riverbed? Do predators swim these rivers?_

features.name: Patient Hunter
features.description: **Spend a Fear** to summon a Glass Snake within Close range of a chosen PC. The Snake appears in or near the river and immediately takes the spotlight to use their "Spinning Serpent" action. _What treasures does the beast have in their burrow? What travelers have already fallen victim to this predator?_

activeElements.impulses: Bar crossing, carry away the unready, divide the land
activeElements.description: A swift-moving river without a bridge crossing, deep enough to sweep away most people.

activeElements.name: Bear

features.name: Overwhelming Force
features.description: Targets who mark HP from the Bear's standard attack are knocked back to Very Close range.

features.name: Bite
features.description: **Mark a Stress** to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal **3d4+10** physical damage and the target is _Restrained_ until they break free with a successful Strength Roll.

features.name: Momentum
features.description: When the Bear makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.

activeElements.description: A large bear with thick fur and powerful claws.
